records.tested_change: Applied the published Appendix B.3/Table 5 polynomial inverse recurrence as a generic dense functional implementation to captured real training covariances and raw gradients. Under a conservative Frobenius-derived spectral bound, 18 of 56 covariance blocks had an eligible published plan; all 18 had float32-MPS spectral inverse residual <=0.00387155 and were within the published residual bound plus 1e-5. The remaining 38 blocks had no eligible plan under this selection policy.
records.scope: Offline capture from the frozen six-layer FP32 byte Transformer harness: widths 256/512, first/last blocks, qkv/proj/fc1/fc2, covariance snapshots at steps 32 and 96; 56 blocks total. CPU float64 selects plans and computes references; generic dense polynomial products run on MPS float32.
limitations: The Frobenius spectral upper bound is conservative; uncovered blocks do not show that the published plans fail there, and tighter certified bounds or additional published plans may change coverage.
This is a functional recurrence check, not an implementation of optimized SYPP kernels and provides no timing, memory, training-quality, time-to-loss or novelty result.
Only 12 of 32 module snapshots had every block covered, so raw preconditioned-gradient comparisons are limited to those modules.
The capture uses full covariance storage and the source harness; the result does not justify a low-rank approximation or a production optimizer change.
Selection was run after captures were available and is not an independent held-out benchmark. No paid API calls or network downloads were used.
